newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel, PLO resume Taba talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO resume Taba talks.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators on Thursday resumed U.S.-mediated talks on a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment in Hebron, officials said.
A senior Israeli official said the sides had begun working in committees at Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba on implementation of issues outstanding from a 1995 interim Israeli-PLO peace deal.
"Israelis want to focus on Hebron and the Palestinians want to focus on other outstanding issues. It will be clear later whether they agree on this," the Israeli official said.
He said Israeli negotiators were "fully prepared" with proposals on how to break an impasse over the West Bank town.
Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour said the PLO was interested in implementation of signed deals and not further proposals.
"We will not listen to any proposal that does not consist of mechanisms of implementing the agreement," Asfour said.
The U.S.-brokered talks are in their second week.
Israelis have sounded notes of optimism that agreement is near but Palestinians have said talks had hit an impasse.
